definition: HIV Resistance Response Database Initiative (RDI) was formed in 2002 to use artificial intelligence (AI) to predict how patients will respond to HIV drugs using data from more 250,000 patients from around 50 countries around the world.
details: The RDI used its models to power its HIV Treatment Response Prediction System (HIV-TRePS). Launched in 2010, this free online tool enabled healthcare professionals to upload their patient’s data and obtain highly accurate predictions of how they would respond to different combinations of the 30 or more drugs available. The tool enabled physicians to individualize their patients’ treatment, using these predictions based on more than a million patient-years of treatment experience. HIV-TRePS was possibly the first ever AI-based system for medical decision-making to be developed, successfully tested, and used in clinical practice. It has since been used by thousands of healthcare professionals to optimise the treatment of tens of thousands of patients. Since the RDI’s inception the treatment of HIV infection has progressed enormously, with more effective and better tolerated drugs available in ever more convenient combination formulations. In most countries HIV is now considered a chronic, manageable condition. Moreover, the success of the drugs in reducing the amount of virus is substantially reducing the onward transmission of the virus and cases of new infections are falling in man

explainer.lead: The HIV Resistance Response Database Initiative was formed in 2002 to use AI to predict how patients respond to HIV drugs, drawing on data from over 250,000 patients in about 50 countries. Its models powered a free clinical prediction tool.

tiers.eli5: Doctors faced a puzzle with dozens of drug combinations, so a large pool of past patient outcomes was used to guess which combination would work for the next patient.
tiers.practitioner: The RDI used its models to power HIV-TRePS, launched in 2010, where clinicians uploaded patient data and received predictions for combinations of the 30 or more available drugs. A pitfall is that predictions rest on over a million patient-years of past treatment experience and are only as good as that data.
tiers.paperLevel: A 2002 initiative using AI to predict patient response to HIV drugs from data on more than 250,000 patients across roughly 50 countries; the models power HIV-TRePS, a free online tool launched in 2010. The definitions provided do not state accuracy figures or model types.

explainer.example: A clinician uploads a patient's data to HIV-TRePS and receives predictions of how that patient would respond to different combinations of the 30 or more available drugs.
